_about: Battle tuning for BattleSim.gd. Started from prototype/battle_core.js; HP x1.6 for longer battles with 2-4 specials each, slime atk raised (6.5) so line/charge mirror matches are ~50/50 with both sides on BattleAI. Tune with tools/run_sims.gd. Times are seconds, distances are field pixels (480x240).
_field_note: background = 480x270 image behind the battle; the 320x180 camera shows y 76-256 of it, so it is mostly ground. field_<name>.png come from tools/make_ground.py (DF-style plain ground: steppe, grass, hall; battle_plains_dusk.png is the older painted one) (horizon at y 104, ground y 104-240, darker HUD strip below); duel_background = painted 480x270 image for the generals' duel (spotlight centred on y 214, where the generals stand, top corners kept dark for the HP bars). Leave either out to get the drawn placeholder.

combat._special_take_note: true = specials are reduced by the target's order/formation damage-taken multipliers (hold, square), like normal hits.

_lanes_note: The field height (y_min..y_max) splits into this many equal lanes, top to bottom. Lane specials hit one lane; the target side dodges by opening it (split).
_commands_note: switch_delay = s the troops stand frozen after an order change (the price of reacting).
_split_note: Open a lane: troops in it step out to the neighbouring lane at speed_mult x their speed, nobody enters it for duration s, everyone hits crowd_atk x while it is open. margin = px around the lane that also counts as inside.
_duel_rules_note: When both armies are gone and both generals stand, the battle cuts to a duel (BattleSim duel section). offer_time = s each side has to choose duel or retreat (undecided = duel; retreat = lose the battle, general survives). Then turns alternate, the faster general first: start_gap s before the first blow, hit_gap s between blows in a turn, turn_gap s between turns. The player only watches.
_general_charge_note: General fights at the front: +mp_on_hit MP per hit it lands, specials launch from where it stands; takes front_take x damage out there, and channel_take x on top while channelling a special; walks back at return_spd_mult x speed when recalled (front_take still applies until it is home). A general never runs from a fight: at its post it never moves (crowding can't shove it), enemy troops spread out around it (front, back, above, below) and it cuts them down one at a time; it ignores the retreat order, and a recall while an enemy is within its reach; with no troops left it walks to the nearest enemy soldier.

_army_size_note: DF-style crowds: 30 troops a side (was 10). Troop hp/atk are 1/3 of the 10-troop values (knight 64/7 -> 21.33/2.33; slime 48 -> 16) so an army weighs the same, radii shrank so the crowd packs closer, specials do damage to troops and damage_general to generals (the old full values), AI unit-count thresholds x3. Slime atk retuned to 1.5 (the old 6.5/3 = 2.17 won ~100%: with 30 a side luck averages out and the stronger side always wins). Mirror line+charge, 200 runs, player vs AI: slime 50.0%, knight 48.5%.

units._ranged_note: Ranged troops (dev mode for now, CLAUDE.md section 4: slime mage, archer), DF style: they stand and shoot from far (reach = range, 240-260 px: from their start spot they reach the enemy front line) at the enemy straight ahead (ranged.aim_y x the usual y weight when picking targets, so they keep to their own row), but are fragile up close: ranged.melee_take = x damage they take from melee hits (shots and specials excluded), and an enemy within close_range gets only a weak point-blank hit (close_mult x). speed = shot px/s (damage lands on arrival, wasted if the target fell), arc = px the shot rises (view only). 100 runs, line, vs AI: slime player charge: spear 30 = 41%, spear 20 + mage 10 = 66%, mage 30 = 98%; hold: 6% / 100% / 100%. Knight player charge: knight 30 = 59%, knight 20 + archer 10 = 56%. All-ranged armies win almost always because the AI has no answer yet (it walks into the shots); tune with run_sims --units= / --enemy-units=.
units._generals_note: Generals start at general_spot behind their army and stay there (hitting only enemies that reach them) until sent in with general_charge; sized so a general-vs-general duel (when all troops are gone) is about even: slime 310 hp / 17 atk vs knight 320 / 18. Each general has a style: front_take = its own damage-taken x when sent in (else general_charge.front_take), ai_charge = how the AI uses it: front (fights at the front from the start), mopup (goes in to finish a beaten army), never. The slime general is a brawler (strong at the front, so it pays more there); the knight general is a commander who should stay back. duel = style in the one-on-one duel (see duel_rules): hits blows per turn of power each (+- jitter share), each landing with chance accuracy. Slime general: two quick, steady blows; knight general: one heavy, swingy blow (same expected damage per turn, roughly)

_orders_note: advance = AI default from the prototype: walks in, no bonuses.
_formations_note: Spots are for an army facing right (left side of the field); a side facing left mirrors x as width - x. flank = extra atk when flank_min or more allies hit the same target. Roles toward generals: general_pull (<1 = enemy general counts as closer when picking targets, applied to squared distance), envelop (px troops swing above/below the enemy general), leash (px troops stay within of their own general). Squads (DF style): guard_share > 0 splits the troops: the first (1 - share) stand on layout.spots as the main group (follows the order), the rest on layout.guard_spots as the guard group: it keeps its spot round its general (and follows it when it goes in), fights only enemies within guard_radius px of it and ignores retreat/hold; on duty it hits guard_atk x and takes guard_take x damage (specials too), dug in round the general. set_guard_out (key R) releases the guards to fight like the main group, or calls them back. layout.groups = [{role: main|guard|raid|div, share, spots}] splits the troops into any groups (first group takes the rounding remainder; div groups are divisions numbered front to back). command (key E): disperse = troops split to the top / bottom lanes leaving the middle open, again = regroup; raid = the raid group runs along the field edge (raid_spd x) to the enemy general, again = call it back; divrush = send the next division in (waiting divisions hold round their own spot and fight enemies within div_radius, with guard_atk / guard_take).

_specials_note: damage = per troop hit, damage_general (optional) = per general hit. Casting pays MP, then telegraph s of warning (target lane shown, general stands still), then the special launches launch_offset px in front of the general (start_x without a general) and sweeps toward the enemy at speed, a band width px deep, hitting each enemy once. lanes 0 = full field height; 1 or 2 = lanes aimed by the caster (AI, or best lane for the player). range = px travelled before it fades; damage drops to min_damage_pct % at the end (no range = full damage to end_x). knockback = px survivors are pushed back. targets: general = a bolt down the enemy general's lane that passes troops (damage to them) but loses block_pct % of its power per troop it goes through, so troops in front shield their general. type guard = defence: after the warning the caster's whole side takes take_mult x damage (specials too) for duration s. type/color are for BattleView; tier/focus are labels (UI, docs).
_tiers_note: Each general has 3 specials (units.<general>.specials = [small, medium, large]). Size rule of thumb: small ~20 MP, 1 s warning, one lane, weakest but hard to dodge; medium ~40 MP, 1.5 s, two lanes or a defence; large ~70 MP, 2 s warning (easiest to dodge), the most power per MP. focus: troops (sweeps soldiers), general (hits the enemy general), defense (guard). A general's focus = what most of its three lean on.

_ai_note: BattleAI, see scripts/battle/BattleAI.gd (same brain for either side). Casting: every think_interval s, hit value per enemy = share of max HP taken + kill_bonus if it dies, general x general_weight; cast when the best lane holds min_share of the value of hitting every enemy; full MP lowers it to full_mp_min_share; own general below danger_hp with enemies within danger_range: any hit, those enemies x danger_weight. Dodging: reaction_time s after an enemy cast, chance dodge_skill: open the lane if it holds dodge_min_units (general = general_weight); full-field special -> full_response order until it passes. General charge (mop-up): after charge_after s, go in at HP >= charge_hp with troop HP >= charge_adv x enemy's and at most charge_max_enemy_troops enemy troops left; come back when troop HP < return_adv x (never for low HP: a general stands and takes the hits, and a recalled one only walks back once nobody is fighting it). Duel offer: retreat if our general needs more than duel_retreat_ratio x the turns theirs needs to win. Three specials: every slot gets the value above (a guard = HP it would save, cast at >= guard_min_value, counting guard_persist of its duration of the fighting now plus enemy specials on their way); of those worth casting, the best value per MP goes, but the AI saves MP (casts nothing) while a dearer one is worth more than save_ratio x per MP, and sticks to that plan; full MP, own general in danger, or an enemy special already coming (guard) end the saving.
_sprites_note: Sprite size standard (pixels at the 480x270 game resolution, shown x3 at 1440x810, x4 at 1080p): troops 32x32 frames, small slime 16x16, generals 48x48. Generals in the duel close-up are drawn at x2 (96 px tall). On the battlefield generals use their optional "field" strips (~34 px tall, made by tools/make_field_sprites.py from the 48 px strips) so they stand at troop scale like Dragon Force instead of towering over the troops; "field" takes dir/frame/foot/height and reuses the anims list. Strips: <dir>/<anim>.png, frames left to right, facing RIGHT. foot = frame pixel that stands on the ground; height = px above the feet for HP bars. Units without sprites use the placeholder shapes. The PNGs in assets/units are placeholders from tools/make_placeholder_sprites.py: replace them with real art of the same frame size.
_fx_sprites_note: Effect strips for specials (BattleView). file = one strip, frames left to right, moving RIGHT (flipped for the side facing left). foot = frame pixel put on the effect's point: wave = crest front on the wave front, base on each lane's bottom edge; hit = centre of the struck unit; launch = the launch point in front of the general. A special lists its effects in "fx": wave / hit / launch for a wave, rider / trail / hit for a charge (rider foot = lance tip on the ground line); anything missing is drawn with the placeholder shapes.
_dev_note: Dev mode (F3 on the setup screen, Battle.gd): pick each side's troops from troop_options (units = [[type, count], ...], front ranks first). For testing troop types before they get real art and balance; run_sims takes the same lists as --units=type:count,... / --enemy-units=...
